title: OpenChainGraph third-party submission manifest
description: Shape of manifest.json, one per submitter directory under ocg-conformance/third-party/<submitter-slug>/. Extends the house ../../vectors/manifest.json entry shape (same six file/hash/execution_hash fields, USERKERNEL-CONFORMANCE-BUILD-SPEC.md section 2) with three 2026 enhancements, each REQUIRED on every entry: a reverse-DNS-style id bound to the submitter's verified GitHub namespace, a machine-readable conformance_witness (CI run hash + fixture digest), and the verbatim trust_disclaimer.

corpus.description: Fixed marker distinguishing this from the house ../../vectors/manifest.json corpus ("ocg-receipt-conformance-vectors").

submitter_namespace.description: MUST equal the sibling submitter.json's namespace field byte-for-byte.

algorithm.description: Restated verbatim from ../../README.md so this manifest is self-describing without requiring a reader to also fetch the house corpus's docs.

id.description: Reverse-DNS-style id: <submitter_namespace>.<kernel-slug>, e.g. io.github.octocat.simple-fee-calculator (2026 enhancement (a), MCP Registry namespace convention). Every roster line is keyed by this id, not by kernel-slug alone, so two submitters can name kernels identically without colliding.

input_file.description: Path relative to this manifest.json, e.g. vectors/inputs/<id-without-namespace-dots>.input.json.

expected_execution_hash.description: SHA-256(JCS({policy_parameters, output_payload})) over the two files above -- the one MANDATORY conformance claim (spec section 1).

source.description: Free text that MUST end with the literal marker "third-party", e.g. "<submitter name>, third-party" -- mirrors the house manifest's source field shape while making provenance unmistakable at a glance.

trust_disclaimer.const: Conformance-suite-pass is not a correctness guarantee, not an endorsement, and not an audit. AINumbers verifies formats; it does not verify facts.
trust_disclaimer.description: Verbatim liability-boundary line (spec section 3.4), repeated on every roster-bound entry -- 2026 enhancement (c). A JSON Schema const, not free text, so it cannot be paraphrased away.

conformance_witness.description: Machine-readable CI-run evidence -- 2026 enhancement (b), the FV-status artifact pattern applied to third-party submissions. This row (USERKERNEL-SCHEMA-1) ships the shape only, with status "pending": no CI Action exists yet to populate it (that is USERKERNEL-CI-1, the next row in the sequence). Once that Action runs against a submission PR, it fills in the remaining fields and flips status to verified or failed.

ci_run_id.description: The CI Action's run identifier (e.g. a GitHub Actions run id). null while status is pending.

ci_run_url.description: Dereferenceable URL to the CI run's logs. null while status is pending.

ci_run_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the CI run's result artifact (its log or structured output), binding this witness to one specific, replayable run rather than a bare unverifiable claim of "CI passed."

fixture_digest.description: SHA-256 over the exact {input_file bytes, expected_output_file bytes} pair the CI run actually checked -- so a later edit to the fixture files invalidates the witness by construction (the digest no longer matches) instead of silently inheriting a stale PASS.

sha256ref.description: A bare 64-hex-char SHA-256 digest, or the same digest with a "sha256:" prefix (matches ../schemas/ocg-receipt-envelope.schema.json's sha256ref shape).
